purpose: Frozen bounded compiler work quotas for language Alpha calibration; a quota is software policy, not a safety theorem or a semantic feature fix.
verification_requirements: Every successful complete compilation runs current independent Verify exactly once, including cached and resident requests.
Analyze and Verify independently establish their existing obligations; neither borrows acceptance from the other.
Source, Types, Analyze, Verify, lowering, machine verification, native execution, failure cleanup and semantic negative controls retain their existing acceptance requirements.
ResourceLimit, Unsupported, cancellation, infrastructure failure, missing execution or zero assertions never count as a positive pass or a semantic-negative pass.
All accepted language and native results must identify the exact source/compiler revision, input identity, selected work profile and all effective Limits.
Standard 10M pressure results and explicit higher-quota historical runs keep separate identities; no historical 50M result becomes a default-policy pass.
Alpha acceptance requires the complete declared positive project set and negative controls on one frozen compiler revision; this profile declaration makes no acceptance claim.

acceptance.functional: A legal original completes independent Verify and the required executions under the published daily CLI profile. A semantic negative must reach its specified rule. Resource exhaustion is an incomplete observation.
acceptance.resource_safety: Published input entrances enforce their selected bounds and stop without Verified output on exhaustion. Check structural limits, compile-time execution limits, and deterministic work exhaustion independently, including fresh requests.
acceptance.calibration: Exact historical implementation step minima and the standard-profile pressure run are recorded separately. A changed minimum alone does not block functional Alpha. A failure under a promised default entrance or a missing required execution remains open.
acceptance.measurements: Report completed executable geometry, physical type preflight visits and peak depth, and cumulative verifier work. Task, CT execution and host memory have separate scopes.
